benchmark.deviation: No total-return index exists in the warehouse (checked 2026-10-22: no TRI/total-return series). The price index understates the benchmark by the dividend yield, roughly 0.1 pp over 20 sessions at a ~1.3% annual yield. This affects only the market-context metric; the PRIMARY test is the paired baseline-vs-tilt difference on an identical universe, where the benchmark does not enter.

comparison.portfolio_b: identical baseline and constraints plus the bounded smart-money overlay
comparison.tilt_scaling: confidence multiplier (high 1.0 / medium 0.6 / low 0.25) x concentration damping (0.5 when single_amc_signal)

cost_model.note: Indian cash-delivery equity. Frozen before any confirmatory run.

execution.entry: open of the first session AFTER the scoring date
execution.exit: open of the session horizon_sessions later

hurdle.note: business acceptance threshold; assessed separately from statistical significance

hypothesis.H0: the smart-money tilt does not produce a positive, deployable incremental net return
hypothesis.H1: the tilt produces positive out-of-sample incremental net return, point estimate >= +1.0 pp over 20 sessions

promotion_rule.failure_policy: no promotion without positive out-of-sample evidence; a failed study is not rescued by changing horizon, benchmark, threshold or subset — that requires a new study_id and a fresh holdout
full_promotion_requires: confidence interval lower bound above zero
promotion_rule.sample_floor_for_review: 12 effectively independent evaluation blocks (a review floor, not a power claim)

statistical_plan.exclusions: every excluded cohort and symbol stored with a reason
statistical_plan.multiple_testing: Holm correction across the two secondary horizons; the primary horizon is fixed at 20 and is not selected post hoc
statistical_plan.outlier_policy: report with and without extremes; the unfiltered result is primary

universe_rule.note: Computed only from sessions on or before the scoring date. Deliberately NOT index membership: nidp.index_constituents has 4 snapshots, so membership-based eligibility would inject survivorship bias. A liquidity rule from prices is reconstructable point-in-time for every date.
